unmapped_findings: At the higher temperature of 600 °C, neither the frequently distributed deformation bands nor the simultaneous deformation-induced ferrite to austenite (DIAT) / austenite to ferrite (DIFT) transformations could be characterized in the deformed microstructure, in contrast to deformation at 500 °C (see Fig. 3e).

The 600 °C condition is the higher-temperature counterpart of the 500 °C/0.6 condition; strain distribution is more homogeneous at 600 °C owing to the higher capability for strain distribution at higher temperature.

The chemical composition (elemental partitioning) SEM analysis reported in Table 1 (Mn 10.3±0.1 / Al 6.0±0.1 wt.% in ferrite and Mn 12.8±0.1 / Al 4.7±0.1 wt.% in austenite) is explicitly stated to be for the specimen deformed at 500 °C, and therefore does not pertain to this 600 °C sample.
